## Overview {#sec-overview}

The goals of this project are twofold. First, the project intends to identify the lifestyle and environmental risk factors associated with Alzheimer's Disease (AD). Second, the project intends to identify which of these lifestyle and environmental risk factors best predict the development of AD beyond genetic and family history risk. To meet these goals, I will use the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center's main dataset, in addition to supplemental PET scan data. I met with Dr. Adam Naj who shared several sources of data I could request online and I spoke with Dr. Christos Davatzikos who pointed me to several of his papers on machine learning modeling in the AD literature. Here is the link to my [final project GitHub repository](https://github.com/npr829/BMIN5030_Final_Project).

## Introduction {#sec-introduction}
In current literature, there is a known association between genetic and family history risk with Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) based on previous studies that have examined these associations via various predictive modeling approaches and observational studies. However, less is known on the association between modifiable risk factors such as lifestyle or environmental factors and the development of AD. Previously, the Lancet published 14 modifiable risk factors with AD and dementia, which included lifestyle factors (e.g., diet, sleep, etc.) and environmental factors (e.g., air pollution). Although, these associations were identified primarily by observational studies. In this study, I propose to use supervised machine learning approaches, specifically, gradient boosted forest trees to create a model that predicts the development of Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) using lifestyle and environmental risk factors. In addition to creating the model, I will identify risk factors that best predict the development of AD beyond genetic and family history risk based on the results of the supervised machine learning.
